pack.name: CKA v1.35: verified labs on K16S
pack.description: The CKA v1.35 track (domains and objectives from the CNCF curriculum) with one verified lab per K16S CKA question: 36 tasks graded on your own lab cluster.
pack.coverage_notes_md: Every competency of the CKA v1.35 curriculum is an objective here; 36 of them have a verified lab (both K16S CKA mocks, by question id). Lessons, questions and flashcards for this track are a separate pack (rex/istari#9). Two labs need the full VM-based K16S install. Task text is never stored in Istari; it is fetched from your instance.

exam_version.name: Certified Kubernetes Administrator (Kubernetes v1.35)
exam_version.format_notes: Performance-based: 15 to 20 command-line tasks on live clusters, two hours, 66% to pass; proctored online. Verified labs here are graded by your K16S instance.

sources.title: Linux Foundation: CKA program changes, effective 2025-02-18

verification.notes: Duration, format and the Kubernetes version come from the Linux Foundation page; the 66% passing score from its candidate instructions. The task count is not published (15 to 20 is typical), so scored_questions is an estimate, not a fact. current_since is 2025-02-18, when the revised curriculum (Helm, Kustomize, the Gateway API, CRDs and operators) took effect per the Linux Foundation notice; a CKA course dated before 2025 teaches the previous curriculum.

objectives.title: Manage role based access control (RBAC)
Prepare underlying infrastructure for installing a Kubernetes cluster
Create and manage Kubernetes clusters using kubeadm
Manage the lifecycle of Kubernetes clusters
Implement and configure a highly-available control plane
Use Helm and Kustomize to install cluster components
Understand extension interfaces (CNI, CSI, CRI, etc.)
Understand CRDs, install and configure operators
Understand application deployments and how to perform rolling update and rollbacks
Use ConfigMaps and Secrets to configure applications
Configure workload autoscaling
Understand the primitives used to create robust, self-healing, application deployments
Configure Pod admission and scheduling (limits, node affinity, etc.)
Understand connectivity between Pods
Define and enforce Network Policies
Use ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer service types and endpoints
Use the Gateway API to manage Ingress traffic
Know how to use Ingress controllers and Ingress resources
Understand and use CoreDNS
Implement storage classes and dynamic volume provisioning
Configure volume types, access modes and reclaim policies
Manage persistent volumes and persistent volume claims
Troubleshoot clusters and nodes
Troubleshoot cluster components
Monitor cluster and application resource usage
Manage and evaluate container output streams
Troubleshoot services and networking

labs.title: A worker node reports NotReady
labs.goals_md: Read the node's conditions and the kubelet's state on the worker, find what stopped it, and bring the node back without rebuilding it.
labs.prerequisites_md: Your K16S instance is up and serves the `cka` profile in the full VM-based install (this task is marked heavy and cannot run under the lightweight mode).
labs.cost_warning_md: Runs on the lab cluster; costs nothing.
labs.steps_md: Set up the environment, work the task in the cluster's terminal, then check. The task text comes from the cluster, live.
labs.expected_observations_md: The node reports Ready and stays Ready; workloads schedule onto it again.
labs.cleanup_md: The next setup resets the environment; nothing to clean by hand.
